name: Veldtmann Pressline Night Shift Full Kit
description: A head-to-toe pressline night crew uniform built for twelve-hour shifts under fluorescent factory light. The core piece is a charcoal-grey ripstop coverall with Veldtmann's orange chevron stripe running diagonally across the chest and left shoulder, embroidered name patch above the right breast pocket, and a corponation logo stamped in heat-transfer vinyl on the back yoke. The coverall features reinforced knee panels in a darker charcoal, triple-stitched seams throughout, and a side-zip aug channel running from the left hip to the mid-calf to accommodate chrome leg prosthetics or exo-brace struts. Underneath sits a Veldtmann-branded moisture-wicking thermal undershirt in slate grey, crew-neck, with flatlock seams to prevent friction burns during long wear. A low-profile hard hat in safety orange clips to a belt loop when not in use. Hands are covered by cut-resistant synth-leather gloves with the fingertips of the dominant hand left open for BCI touchpad operation.
functionality: aug-channel side zip for chrome leg accommodation, reinforced knee panels, BCI-open fingertip gloves, tool loops at hip and thigh, chest and hip pockets with magnetic closures, hard hat clip loop, moisture-wicking underlayer
what_it_says: This is someone who shows up, clocks in, and does the work. The name patch and corponation branding say they belong to a machine — not proudly, not bitterly, just practically. The immaculate condition of the coverall despite its age signals discipline and a certain quiet dignity.
story_hooks: A worker's name patch belongs to someone who died on the floor three months ago — and they're still wearing it because no one updated the system.
The aug-channel zip conceals a smuggled data chip sewn into the lining, passed between shifts by workers organizing against Veldtmann's new productivity quotas.
A supervisor notices the corponation logo has been subtly defaced on a worker's back yoke — a small act of resistance that could mean termination or worse.

physical_description.visual_profile: A utilitarian full-body pressline uniform that reads as industrial-grade and purposeful. The charcoal-grey coverall dominates with a striking diagonal orange chevron stripe cutting across the chest, creating visual flow and authority. When worn, the silhouette is functional and blocky—designed for movement and tool access rather than aesthetics. The ensemble projects Tier 3 working-class competence: a person built for twelve-hour shifts under factory fluorescents.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed through the torso and thighs to accommodate layering and equipment, with tapered leg openings designed to fit over boots or augmentation interfaces. The cut prioritizes range of motion and durability over form-fitting. Sleeves sit at the wrist with reinforced cuffs.
physical_description.primary_material: Charcoal ripstop nylon coverall with moisture-wicking slate-grey thermal base layer underneath. Gloves are cut-resistant synth-leather with exposed fingertips on the dominant hand for BCI interaction.
physical_description.texture: The ripstop weave has a subtle dimpled surface—practical and slightly stiff when new, breaking in to a softer drape after weeks of shift work. Reinforced knee panels feel thicker, almost textile armor. Flatlock seams on the undershirt are smooth against skin. Synth-leather gloves have a matte finish with subtle grip texture on the palms.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary charcoal grey with safety-orange chevron stripe and accent trim. Low-profile hard hat in high-visibility orange. Undershirt in slate grey. Gloves in dark synth-leather brown.
physical_description.closures: Heavy-duty YKK side zip running hip to mid-calf (aug channel). Center front oversized two-way zipper on coverall for quick changes. Magnetic snaps on chest pocket flaps. Belt loops for hard-hat attachment. Glove wrist closures are friction-fit elastic cuffs.
distinctive_features: Embroidered name patch above right breast pocket
Heat-transfer vinyl corporation logo on back yoke
Reinforced knee panels in darker charcoal
Integrated side-zip aug channel for chrome prosthetics/exo-braces
Cut-resistant synth-leather gloves with open fingertips on dominant hand
Detachable safety-orange hard hat clipped to belt loop
Multiple chest and hip pockets for tools and small components
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3 working-class. High-quality industrial apparel issued or purchased by factory workers, technicians, and pressline operators. Not cheap enough to be Tier 5 salvage, not premium enough to be corpo-grade Tier 1.
physical_description.cultural_context: Wearing this signals you are a skilled factory worker, likely in the GLMZ's pressline or heavy manufacturing sector. The Veldtmann branding suggests either direct employment or freelance contract work. The aug channel indicates you're either cybernetically enhanced or prepared to be. This is the uniform of the industrial backbone—reliable, unadorned, and purposeful.
physical_description.condition_typical: When new: crisp, stiff, ink-bright chevron stripe. After weeks of shifts: broken-in, slightly faded orange from sweat and factory chemicals, minor stains and scuffs on knee panels and glove fingertips, wrinkles setting into the fabric from repeated movement. Name patch slightly worn at the edges. Hard hat may have small dents or scratches from worksite use.
